newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher after early decline.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher after early decline.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly higher on Wednesday recovering from early losses led by a rise in medium-capitalization stocks, dealers said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.11 percent, or 0.22 points, to 203.26 on all-share turnover of 72 million shekels against 69 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 0.20 percent to 211.81.
"The session opened with a mild decline and the indices fell by 0.4 percent. By midday the trend changed and the market recovered," said Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex Securities.

"The big institutional investors are trying to prevent the market from falling by buying shares," said Michael Weiss of Evergreen Capital Markets, who said most of the activity was concentrated in the medium-capitalization stocks.
"I belive that if nothing dramatic happens the market will remain stable until the end of the year," Weiss said.

But Nahum said he was more optimistic. "The recovery of the market today is another sign of the market's strength. The fact that the Maof index is still above 210 after several days of profit-taking is another positive indicator," he said.
Elite Industries led the most actives, rising 3.75 percent to 1,659 on volume of 4.7 million shekels. Traders said the share rose following big off-the-floor transactions made today.
Elbit, the main losser on the Maof, fell 3.75 percent to 2,393 on volume of only 83,676 shekels.

Other active shares included Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which lost 1.25 percent to 147,302 on volume of 4.3 million shekels, and Blue Square Stores, which fell 1.0 percent to 2,536 on turnover of 3.2 million shekels.
